_comment: Manual import specifications. Each spec defines the target record type, expected columns with accepted aliases, user-facing step-by-step instructions, and an example. Column matching is case/space/punctuation-insensitive.

specs.name: KeepTradeCut Values

columns.description: Player name, or a pick label such as '2027 Early 1st' / '2027 Pick 1.04'
QB/RB/WR/TE/RDP (RDP or PICK = rookie draft pick)

instructions: Open https://keeptradecut.com/dynasty-rankings (or /fantasy-rankings for redraft) in your browser.
Choose the format that matches your league: 1QB or Superflex (and TE premium if applicable).
KTC does not offer an export button and its Terms prohibit automated collection, so this app never downloads KTC data for you.
Record the players you care about (or the full list) into a spreadsheet with at least two columns: Player and Value. Optional: Position, Team, Age, Rank.
For draft picks use the exact KTC label in the Player column, e.g. '2027 Early 1st', '2027 Mid 2nd', '2028 1st'.
Save the spreadsheet as CSV (File → Download/Save As → CSV).
Return here, click 'Choose File' and select the CSV.
Set 'Ranking type' and 'QB format' to match what you copied.
Confirm the detected column mapping, review the preview and the unmatched-player report.
Click 'Import'. Values are stored as the 'KeepTradeCut' market source and the model recalculates.
specs.example_csv:
Player,Position,Team,Age,Value
Ja'Marr Chase,WR,CIN,26.6,9998
Bijan Robinson,RB,ATL,24.7,9750
2027 Early 1st,RDP,,,6400
2028 1st,RDP,,,5600

specs.name: FantasyPros Rankings (CSV export)

columns.description: Position or positional rank like 'RB12' (the position part is extracted)

instructions: Sign in at https://www.fantasypros.com (a free account is sufficient for most rankings pages).
Open the rankings page you want, e.g. NFL → Rankings → Rest of Season (PPR) or Dynasty → Overall / Superflex / Rookies.
Select the scoring format that matches your league (Standard / Half PPR / PPR).
Use the page's Download/Export option (CSV) if your account offers it; otherwise select the rankings table, copy it, paste it into a spreadsheet and save as CSV.
Make sure the CSV has a rank column (RK or ECR) and a player column (Player Name).
Return here, click 'Choose File' and select the CSV.
Set 'Ranking type', 'QB format' and 'List scope' to match the page you exported.
Confirm the detected columns (e.g. 'RK' → rank, 'PLAYER NAME' → player_name, 'POS' → position).
Review the preview, duplicates and unmatched-player report.
Click 'Import'. The list is stored under 'FantasyPros (manual export)' and used as a consensus signal.

specs.name: Projections (FFToday or any site)

columns.description: Only used for K/DEF or when stat columns are missing (assumed to be in YOUR league's scoring).

instructions: Open a projections page you are allowed to use, e.g. https://www.fftoday.com/rankings/ (Projections → Rest of Season or Season).
Pick one position at a time if the site splits projections by position (recommended — mixed-position tables often share column names).
Copy the table into a spreadsheet. Keep the header row. Include a Position column (add one if the site omits it, e.g. fill 'RB').
Keep the raw stat columns (Pass Yds, Pass TD, INT, Rush Yds, Rush TD, Rec, Rec Yds, Rec TD …). The app re-scores them with YOUR league scoring, so a fantasy-points column is optional.
Save as CSV.
Return here, click 'Choose File', select the CSV and set 'Projection scope'.
Confirm the column mapping — check that passing and rushing yards were not swapped (sites often label both 'Yds').
Review the preview and the unmatched-player report, then click 'Import'.
specs.example_csv:
Player,Position,Team,G,Rush Att,Rush Yds,Rush TD,Rec,Rec Yds,Rec TD
Bijan Robinson,RB,ATL,14,240,1100,9,50,420,2

specs.name: Trade Values (generic)
instructions: Use any trade-value chart you are permitted to use. The scale does not matter (the model maps values by rank onto its own scale).
Create a CSV with at least Player and Value columns. Higher value must mean a more valuable player.
Choose the value type (Dynasty/Redraft) and QB format that the chart was built for.
Choose File → confirm mapping → review → Import.

specs.name: Rankings (generic)
instructions: Use any ranking list you trust (an analyst's column, your own rankings, a league-mate's sheet).
Make a CSV with Rank and Player columns (Position strongly recommended).
Choose File → set ranking type/QB format → confirm mapping → review → Import.

specs.name: ADP (generic)
instructions: Export or copy ADP from your draft platform or an ADP site (e.g. Underdog, Sleeper, FFC).
Make a CSV with Player and ADP columns (decimal overall pick, e.g. 14.3).
Choose File → set draft format → confirm mapping → review → Import.

specs.name: Rookie Pick Values (generic)
instructions: Use any pick-value chart you are permitted to use.
Make a CSV with a Pick column and a Value column. Supported labels: '2027 1.04', '2027 Pick 1.04', '2027 Early 1st', '2027 1st (Late)', '2028 1st', '2029 2nd'.
Choose File → set QB format → confirm mapping → review → Import.
